name: Dabchick
alt: A green narrowboat with a bicycle and pots of herbs on its roof, moored below a brick bridge
blurb: The smallest of the six, and the one a single person can work through a lock without shouting for help. Two people, a double bed that stays made up, and room on the roof for the bikes.
features: Fixed double bed
Solid-fuel stove and diesel heating
Full-size fridge, gas hob and oven
Pump-out toilet, hot shower
Roof rack for two bicycles

name: Kingfisher
alt: The roof of a blue narrowboat seen from above, cruising a wide stretch of river
blurb: Four berths in 52 feet, which is the length most first-timers should hire. Short enough to turn in any winding hole on the Oxford, long enough that the twin cabin is not a cupboard.
features: Double cabin and a twin cabin with a door
Solid-fuel stove and diesel heating
Dinette that converts to a bed if you are five
Shower and toilet, separate from the galley
Dogs welcome

name: Moorhen
alt: Two dark-hulled narrowboats moored in dappled shade under trees
blurb: Two proper double cabins, one at each end, so two couples can both shut a door. The extra five feet over Kingfisher goes into a galley with real worktop. No dogs aboard: the cabin floors are bare wood.
features: Two double cabins, one at each end
Solid-fuel stove and diesel heating
Long galley with oven and four-ring hob
Walk-through bathroom with a full shower
Bare timber floors, so no dogs

name: Reed Warbler
bathrooms: Shower and toilet, plus a second toilet
alt: A green-and-cream narrowboat passing through a raised lift bridge, the steerer smiling at the tiller
blurb: Sixty feet is the longest hull that fits every winding hole on the northern routes, so Reed Warbler is our family boat: six berths, a second toilet, and a cratch at the front for wet coats.
features: Double cabin and two twin cabins
Second toilet, so nobody queues
Solid-fuel stove and diesel heating
Covered cratch for coats and boots
Dogs welcome

name: Grey Heron
alt: A red-and-green narrowboat cruising away down a rippling canal, the steerer at the back
blurb: Sixty-eight feet, eight people, two shower rooms. She is too long to turn above Twyford Wharf, so she goes south to Oxford and north to Banbury and never further without a conversation with us first.
features: Two double cabins and two twin cabins
Two shower rooms
Solid-fuel stove and diesel heating
Saloon with a table that seats eight
Too long for the northern winding holes

name: Mute Swan
alt: A black narrowboat with a red-and-white striped bow, moored by a brick wharf cottage
blurb: The longest boat the Oxford Canal locks will take: seventy feet, ten berths, and a steerer who has done the handover with us twice. We will not hand her to a crew without an experienced helm.
features: Three double cabins and two twin cabins
Two shower rooms, three toilets
Solid-fuel stove and diesel heating
Seventy feet: the limit of the Oxford locks
Handover is two hours, not one
